{"analyses":[{"paper_id":"doi-10-15760-mcnair-2019-13-1-2","title":"Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in Three Registers of English","research_question":"How do the distribution, referential functions, pronoun choices, and non-nominal antecedent properties of abstract pronominal anaphora vary across newswire, spontaneous dialogue, and planned speech?","methodology":"O'Donnell compiled a corpus spanning newswire text, spontaneous dialogue, and planned speech. All instances of the pronouns \"it\", \"this\", and \"that\" were annotated, together with their non-nominal antecedents when present. The study compared pronoun frequencies, referential functions, and grammatical characteristics of non-nominal antecedents across the three registers; only the abstract was accessible, so sample sizes, detailed coding procedures, and statistical analyses could not be inspected.","key_findings":[{"finding":"The frequencies of different referential functions vary across the three registers.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"Pronoun choice and the referential function served by a pronoun vary by register.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The grammatical structures of non-nominal antecedents vary across the text types.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The difficulty of annotating the relevant anaphoric phenomena varies across the material studied.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The authors conclude that spoken discourse exhibits a range of pronominal reference and non-nominal antecedent patterns that may not be recoverable from even very large newswire collections.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The accessible abstract provides no empirical analysis of multi-question messages, unanswered subquestions, scoped approval or rejection, or proposition-level reply-to alignment.","evidence_type":"unsupported","section":"Abstract (scope)"}],"limitations":["Only the abstract could be read because the repository's full-text download returned HTTP 403, so detailed corpus size, annotation agreement, statistical tests, and numerical results could not be verified.","The study compares linguistic registers rather than workplace email or enterprise communication specifically.","Its central relation is pronominal anaphora between a pronoun and an antecedent, not the scope of a reply over one or more propositions in a prior message.","Although spontaneous dialogue is included, the accessible abstract does not indicate that multi-question turns, unanswered questions, approvals, rejections, or multi-antecedent response links were separately annotated.","The accessible source does not establish public availability of the compiled corpus or research code."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":false,"dataset_available":false,"metrics_reported":false},"confidence_scores":{"register_variation":0.99,"pronoun_function_variation":0.98,"antecedent_structure_variation":0.98,"spoken_vs_newswire_difference":0.97,"partial_reply_scope_not_demonstrated":0.96},"raw_claims":["Abstract anaphora can refer to discourse entities such as events, facts, and propositions.","Abstract-anaphora antecedents can have non-nominal syntactic structure.","The corpus combines newswire, spontaneous dialogue, and planned speech.","The pronouns \"it\", \"this\", and \"that\" were annotated throughout the corpus.","Non-nominal antecedents associated with those pronouns were also annotated.","The study compares pronoun frequency, referential function, and antecedent characteristics across registers.","Multiple aspects of abstract-pronoun usage differ between the three registers.","The accessible abstract does not report an annotation of reply scope between questions and answers."],"source_url":"https://pdxscholar.library.pdx.edu/mcnair/vol13/iss1/2/","access":"abstract_only"},{"paper_id":"2306.15103","title":"Structured Dialogue Discourse Parsing","research_question":"Can dialogue discourse parsing be improved by globally and jointly learning discourse links and relation labels as a structured labeled multi-root non-projective spanning tree rather than making independent local decisions?","methodology":"The authors formulate a dialogue's discourse structure as a labeled directed multi-root non-projective spanning tree, jointly scoring links and their discourse relations with structured encoding and matrix-tree learning and performing structured inference with a modified Chiu-Liu-Edmonds procedure. The model uses pretrained language representations and contextual encoding without explicit hand-crafted speaker or turn-relation features. It is evaluated in-domain and cross-domain on STAC game dialogues and Molweni, derived from Ubuntu IRC technical discussions, using UAS/Link F1 and LAS/Link-and-Relation F1, with reported main results averaged over three runs. Additional analyses examine dialogue length, individual relation types, and robustness when speaker and turn information is removed.","key_findings":[{"finding":"The proposed parser reaches LAS 59.6 on STAC and 59.9 on Molweni, improving over the previous best results by 2.3 and 1.5 points respectively.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"5.4 Main Results - In-domain"},{"finding":"In cross-domain evaluation, the method obtains LAS 38.0 for STAC-to-Molweni and 31.6 for Molweni-to-STAC, beating the best compared baselines by 5.1 and 4.8 points respectively, although it is not best on cross-domain UAS.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"5.4 Main Results - Cross-domain"},{"finding":"The structured parser's performance degrades less than baseline parsers as dialogues become longer.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"5.5 Additional Analyses - Dialogue Length Robustness"},{"finding":"The structured method improves correct predictions for relations including QA_pair and Comment on STAC and QA_pair and Clarification Question on Molweni, while low-resource relations remain difficult.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"5.5 Additional Analyses - Relation Performance Breakdown"},{"finding":"Removing speaker and turn information reduces STAC LAS from 59.6 to 54.4 for the proposed parser, compared with 57.3 to 47.8 for the Struct-Aware baseline.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"5.5 Additional Analyses - Speaker and Turn Feature Robustness"},{"finding":"The tree conversion does not retain all multi-parent discourse links: 6% of STAC edges are discarded, and when a node has more than one parent only the latest parent is retained; Molweni requires no such edge removal.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"3 Structure Formulation"},{"finding":"Consequently, the evaluated representation does not directly preserve a response EDU that is jointly attached to multiple antecedent propositions, and the experiments do not separately measure multi-question partial replies, unanswered subquestions, or scoped approval or rejection.","evidence_type":"unsupported","section":"3 Structure Formulation; 5 Experiments"}],"limitations":["The tree constraint forces each non-root node to a single retained parent, so genuine multi-parent discourse attachment is lost in the transformed STAC data.","The paper assumes elementary discourse units are already segmented rather than evaluating proposition or EDU segmentation jointly with attachment.","The evaluated units are dialogue EDUs or utterances, not explicitly proposition-level components within a multi-question email message.","Neither STAC nor Molweni is a workplace-email corpus; STAC is game chat and Molweni is based on technical Ubuntu IRC discussions.","The evaluation does not report dedicated measures for unanswered questions, partially answered multi-question turns, or the scope of approval and rejection acts.","Low-resource discourse-relation types remain difficult.","Cross-domain UAS results are not uniformly better than older baselines, so the improvement is strongest for joint link-and-relation prediction rather than link prediction alone."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"in_domain_las_gain":0.99,"cross_domain_las_gain":0.99,"long_dialogue_robustness":0.96,"qa_relation_improvement":0.97,"single_parent_tree_constraint":1.0,"multi_antecedent_reply_gap":0.99,"partial_reply_scope_gap":0.98},"raw_claims":["Dialogue discourse parsing predicts both links between discourse units and labels for those links.","The method globally models dialogue structure with a latent tree distribution rather than treating every link independently.","STAC contains multiparty online-game dialogue, whereas Molweni is based on Ubuntu IRC technical discussion.","UAS evaluates link existence, while LAS requires both the link and its relation label to be correct.","The proposed system reports 74.4 UAS and 59.6 LAS on STAC in-domain evaluation.","It reports 83.5 UAS and 59.9 LAS on Molweni in-domain evaluation.","The main table reports averages over three runs.","Six percent of STAC graph edges are removed to obtain the tree-like training structure.","For a node with multiple annotated parents, only the latest parent is kept.","QA_pair is among the relations for which the structured parser improves over the comparison baseline.","The study models dialogue-level attachment but does not evaluate proposition-level completeness of replies to multi-part questions."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2306.15103","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"manual-e4d6ad7ca1","title":"Anaphoric Annotation in the ARRAU Corpus","research_question":"Can an anaphora annotation scheme represent ambiguous interpretations, multiple antecedents, and discourse deixis to abstract clause-level antecedents with useful human agreement across dialogue and written genres?","methodology":"The authors developed ARRAU through a series of annotation experiments, often using MMAX2, in which multiple annotators independently marked anaphoric phenomena and agreement was assessed with measures including Krippendorff's alpha. The resulting corpus combines task-oriented TRAINS dialogues, Pear Stories, GNOME texts, and Wall Street Journal material; noun phrases are markables and clauses can serve as potential antecedents for discourse deixis. The scheme uses pointers from anaphoric expressions to antecedents, permits multiple pointers for plural antecedents, separate pointer sets for ambiguous interpretations, and pointers from referring noun phrases to clauses introducing events, actions, or plans. The paper reports corpus composition and summarizes preliminary use of the annotations in anaphora-resolution experiments.","key_findings":[{"finding":"Agreement on anaphoric chains in the reported annotation experiments was approximately alpha 0.6-0.7.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"3 Agreement on ambiguity and discourse deixis"},{"finding":"For discourse deixis, annotators tended to agree on the general antecedent region but disagreed about exact boundaries, yielding agreement around alpha 0.55.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"3 Agreement on ambiguity and discourse deixis"},{"finding":"The annotation experiments motivated constraining discourse-deixis antecedent regions to predefined clause-level units and distinguishing plural multi-antecedent cases from genuinely ambiguous alternative interpretations.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"3 Agreement on ambiguity and discourse deixis"},{"finding":"The reported corpus contains 110 texts and 94,212 words, including 455 markables pointing to textual regions and 103 explicitly ambiguous markables.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"4.1 Composition, Table 1"},{"finding":"ARRAU can encode several antecedents for a plural anaphoric expression and can encode two alternative sets of antecedent pointers for ambiguity.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"4.2 Annotation scheme"},{"finding":"Reference to an abstract event, action, or plan is represented by linking the referring noun phrase to the clause introducing that abstract entity.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"4.2 Annotation scheme"},{"finding":"The paper does not annotate conversational reply-to relations, proposition-level answer scope, unanswered subquestions, or scoped approval and rejection; its multiple-antecedent mechanism concerns anaphoric reference rather than a response jointly answering multiple propositions.","evidence_type":"unsupported","section":"4.2 Annotation scheme; 7 Conclusions"}],"limitations":["Human agreement is only moderate for anaphoric chains and lower for the exact boundaries of discourse-deictic antecedents, showing that scope annotation is intrinsically difficult.","The corpus contains task-oriented dialogue but is not a workplace-email or enterprise-messaging corpus.","Clause-level discourse-deixis antecedents identify what an anaphoric expression refers to; they do not encode which prior questions or propositions a reply answers.","Multiple antecedent pointers principally represent plural reference, while separate pointer sets represent ambiguity, so they should not be interpreted as empirical evidence about one reply jointly responding to several propositions.","The preliminary system experiment converted richer pointer structures into equivalence sets and selected the first interpretation for ambiguous anaphors, losing some of the annotation's complexity.","At the time described by the paper, a first corpus release had been completed and used in a workshop, but the paper only states an intention to make the corpus publicly available before LREC, so public dataset availability is not established by this source.","The paper summarizes agreement results partly from earlier experiments rather than reporting a fresh comprehensive reliability analysis for every corpus genre."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":false,"dataset_available":false,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"anaphoric_chain_agreement":0.99,"discourse_deixis_agreement":0.99,"multi_antecedent_annotation":1.0,"clause_level_abstract_antecedents":1.0,"corpus_composition":0.99,"reply_scope_gap":0.99,"workplace_email_gap":0.99},"raw_claims":["ARRAU was designed to cover ambiguous anaphoric expressions and references to abstract entities.","Its genres include TRAINS task-oriented dialogue as well as narrative and written text.","As many as twenty annotators participated independently in some annotation experiments.","Anaphoric-chain agreement was reported in roughly the 0.6-0.7 alpha range.","Discourse-deixis antecedent boundaries produced agreement of about 0.55 alpha.","All clauses are treated as potential antecedents for discourse deixis.","Multiple pointers from one expression can encode plural antecedents.","Two distinct pointer sets can encode alternative interpretations of an ambiguous expression.","An event, action, or plan reference can point from a noun phrase to the clause introducing the abstract entity.","Table 1 reports 110 texts and 94,212 words in the corpus.","The annotation scheme does not define a question-answer completeness or partial-reply relation."],"source_url":"https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220745830_Anaphoric_Annotation_in_the_ARRAU_Corpus","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"manual-b0133009f6","title":"The CODI-CRAC 2022 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue","research_question":"How effectively can systems identify and resolve identity anaphora, bridging references, and discourse deixis across several dialogue domains under predicted-mention, gold-mention, and gold-anaphor evaluation conditions?","methodology":"CODI-CRAC 2022 rechecked data from the previous shared task, annotated new test material from AMI, LIGHT, PERSUASION, and SWITCHBOARD using the ARRAU-style MMAX2 scheme, and used ARRAU material including TRAINS as additional training data. Every newly annotated document was assigned to at least two annotators, and the resulting data were converted to the CONLL-UA Extended format. Systems were evaluated separately on identity anaphora, bridging, and discourse deixis with the Universal Anaphora scorer; bridging and discourse deixis were tested under predicted-mention, gold-mention, and gold-anaphor settings. The overview reports results from 230 runs submitted by three teams and compares them with task baselines.","key_findings":[{"finding":"The new dialogue datasets comprise 218 documents and 214,625 tokens across AMI, LIGHT, PERSUASION, and SWITCHBOARD, with 1,583 discourse-deixis instances reported in Table 1.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"3.4 The Corpus, Table 1"},{"finding":"Participant systems outperform the supplied baselines on virtually all shared-task settings.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"8 Results; 9 Conclusion and Future Work"},{"finding":"For discourse deixis, the best UTD_NLP system obtains macro-average CoNLL F1 of 48.69 with predicted mentions, 49.56 with gold mentions, and 66.66 when gold anaphors and mentions are supplied, while the corresponding baselines score 14.56, 23.15, and 42.28.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"8.3 Task 3 - Discourse Deixis, Table 5"},{"finding":"The substantial improvement under the gold-anaphor condition indicates that identifying which expressions are discourse-deictic remains a major difficulty, not merely selecting their antecedents.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"8.3 Task 3 - Discourse Deixis"},{"finding":"For bridging, supplying gold anaphors produces a much larger gain than supplying gold mentions alone; the best macro-average rises from 25.94 in Gold M to 46.87 in Gold A.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"8.2 Task 2 - Bridging Anaphora, Table 4"},{"finding":"AMI is substantially harder than the other corpora for identity anaphora and bridging, which the authors attribute mainly to its longer conversations and longer distances between anaphors and antecedents.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"8.1 Task 1; 9 Conclusion and Future Work"},{"finding":"Identity evaluation includes split-antecedent anaphora, but split antecedents denote entity sets composed from separately introduced noun phrases rather than a reply jointly attached to multiple antecedent propositions.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"2 Background; 4.2 Evaluation Settings"},{"finding":"The shared task provides no dedicated annotation or metric for multi-question partial replies, unanswered subquestions, scoped approval or rejection, or proposition-level response-to links.","evidence_type":"unsupported","section":"4 Task Description"}],"limitations":["The shared task studies anaphoric interpretation rather than conversational reply scope, so discourse-deixis links should not be treated as equivalent to question-answer or approval-scope links.","None of the four new evaluation domains is an email corpus; AMI provides meeting dialogue but does not by itself establish evidence about workplace email behavior.","Split-antecedent identity coreference concerns plural entities, not a response jointly addressing multiple proposition antecedents.","The task does not label whether individual subquestions in a multi-question message were answered or left unanswered.","Approval and rejection acts are not separately represented as scoped responses to antecedent propositions.","Data access is heterogeneous: AMI, LIGHT, and PERSUASION are described as freely available through the shared-task site, whereas ARRAU and SWITCHBOARD are distributed through LDC with access conditions.","Only three teams participated, despite the large number of submitted runs, limiting the diversity of system approaches represented.","The paper contains a small internal count discrepancy: the prose reports 60,993 total markables for the new datasets while Table 1 reports 60,933."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"corpus_scale":0.99,"systems_beat_baselines":0.99,"discourse_deixis_results":1.0,"anaphor_identification_bottleneck":0.98,"bridging_gold_anaphor_gain":1.0,"ami_length_effect":0.94,"split_antecedent_scope_distinction":0.99,"partial_reply_scope_gap":0.99},"raw_claims":["The shared task evaluates identity anaphora, bridging reference, and discourse deixis in dialogue.","New annotations use conversation data from AMI, LIGHT, PERSUASION, and SWITCHBOARD.","TRAINS dialogue from ARRAU is included in the training material.","Every newly annotated document was annotated by at least two annotators.","Table 1 reports 218 new-data documents containing 214,625 tokens.","AMI consists of long multiparty meeting recordings.","The Universal Anaphora scorer is used for evaluation.","Identity evaluation includes split-antecedent cases.","Discourse-deixis evaluation separates predicted-mention, gold-mention, and gold-anaphor conditions.","The best reported discourse-deixis system reaches a macro-average F1 of 66.66 when gold anaphors are supplied.","Participant systems outperform the discourse-deixis baseline by large margins.","The paper does not define a proposition-level partial-answer relation for multi-question turns."],"source_url":"https://aclanthology.org/2022.codi-crac.1.pdf","access":"full_text"}],"skipped":[]}
